cards.text: Jesus just took a synagogue leader's daughter by the hand, the girl got up, and the news spread through all that region. Now, as Jesus goes on from there, two blind men follow Him, crying out. Friend, they can't SEE Him and they're still keeping up, while I lose track of a cookie tray I'm HOLDING.

cards.question: As the two blind men follow Jesus, what are they crying out for?

cards.text: 'Have mercy on us, Son of David!' Not 'Teacher,' not 'sir,' but a name that points all the way back to David, Israel's king.

cards.question: Jesus goes inside a house. The two blind men give up and stay outside.

cards.text: Nope, they come right in to Him, and they STILL find Him while I can't find a rolling pin in my own bakery with the lights ON. Before Jesus does anything, He asks them one question.

cards.question: Before He heals the two blind men, what does Jesus ask them?

answers.text: Do you believe that I am able to do this
How long have you both been blind
Who told you where to find Me

cards.text: No hemming, no hawing. 'Yes, Lord,' they answer, and Jesus touches their eyes.

cards.question: As He touches their eyes, Jesus tells the two men it will be done to them according to their ___.

cards.text: Their eyes are OPENED! And the very next thing Jesus does is get stern with them.

cards.question: What does Jesus sternly warn the two men He just healed?

answers.text: See that no one finds out about this
Go and show yourselves to the priest
Follow Me wherever I go from here

cards.question: The two healed men do what Jesus says and keep the news to themselves.

cards.text: They go out and spread the news about Him through the WHOLE land. Friend, I can't keep quiet about a batch that came out perfectly round, and these men just got their EYES back.
As they're leaving, people bring another man to Jesus. This one has a demon, and he can't speak.

cards.question: When the demon is driven out, the man who couldn't speak begins to talk.
When the man starts talking, the crowds watching are ___.

cards.text: The crowds say, “Nothing like this has ever been seen in Israel!” The man who couldn't say a word is talking, and now the WHOLE crowd is talking.
But not everybody's cheering. The Pharisees, a group of Jewish religious leaders, see the same thing and come up with an explanation of their own.

cards.question: What do the Pharisees say about how Jesus drives out demons?

answers.text: It is by the prince of demons
It is by the power of Elijah
It is by magic learned in Egypt

findings.problem: Card 1 cites Matthew 9:25-27, but its fact that the girl is a synagogue leader's daughter comes from Matthew 9:18 ("a synagogue leader came and knelt before Him"). Verses 9:25-26 only say "the girl." The citation should run from the first verse the card uses. Alternatively, drop "synagogue leader's" so the card uses only 9:25-27.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Card 17's setup, "But not everybody's cheering," tells the baker that the Pharisees' explanation is hostile. That rules out the wrong answer on card 18, "It is by the power of Elijah," which would credit Jesus with a prophet's power. Only the right answer and "magic learned in Egypt" fit the setup. The fix is either to replace the Elijah answer with another hostile-sounding explanation or to soften the setup line.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Card 5 repeats the joke from card 1 with the same structure. Card 1 says they can't see but keep up, while Papa Dorin loses a tray he's holding. Card 5 says they still find Jesus, while Papa Dorin can't find a rolling pin with the lights on. Both jokes also turn on the men's blindness. Each joke is self-deprecating and respectful on its own. No rule addresses reusing a joke within one stop, or how often a person's disability can be the setup for a comparison.
findings.question: Should Papa Dorin avoid repeating the same joke setup within a stop? And should jokes that contrast a Bible character's disability with his own clumsiness be limited or avoided, even when they are respectful?
